conviction_note: The fiscal Q4 print should land close to the bar the company set itself (Q4 guided down double digits with margins flat year on year). The stock trades on the first FY27 guide. The industry's own forecast from 16 October (285k units in 2027, flat to down) sits below consensus FY27 revenue of +3.7% and EPS of +34%, which points to a guide under consensus. Against that, the stock is down 19% in 20 days and 30% since mid-August, it sits 0.7% above its 52-week low, and it rose on both of its last two guide events (+28.5% on the first FY26 guide, +13.2% on the June guide cut). So the negative guidance read largely agrees with the 5.9-point put skew and the run-up, and I set p_up at 49, near a coin flip. abs_move is 11, the option-implied event move. The findings sum to +0.1 and the scaled number is -0.22: both are near zero and they do not disagree.
bar: Q4 FY26 (Jun-Aug 2026): adjusted EPS consensus $0.46-0.50 (TipRanks 0.46, Benzinga 0.49, sweep/EarningsWhispers ~0.50; https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WGO/earnings-forecasts) and revenue ~$665M (Benzinga, single source). This sits inside the company's implied Q4 range from the FY26 guide of $2.65-2.75B / adj EPS $1.65-2.00 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000107687/000162828026045356/exh9912026q3earningsrelease.htm). Nine-month revenue is $2,058.8M and nine-month adj EPS $1.31, so Q4 implies $591-691M and $0.34-0.69. On the Q3 call the CFO said Q4 sales would be down sequentially and down double digits year on year, with gross and EBITDA margins 'flattish to last year' (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/WGO/Q32026). FY27 consensus is adj EPS $2.39 and revenue $2.82B, 14 analysts, updated 2026-10-13 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/wgo/forecast/). That FY27 bar has one source, so the guidance finding is capped.
positioning_check: MarketBeat, record date 2026-09-30 (published 2026-10-09): 2,686,960 shares short, 9.99% of float, 4.2 days to cover, up 5.5% from the prior period (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/WGO/short-interest/). Moderate, not crowded. The baseline has 25-delta skew at +5.88 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.88, an event-implied move of 11.07% and the ATM spread at 21% of mid (thin options). The stock is down 19.2% over 20 days, 0.73% above its 52-week low and 54% below its 52-week high. The CEO sold 12,045 shares at $32.68 on 2026-08-13 under a 10b5-1 plan (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000107687/000180809626000006/form4-08312026_020830.xml); the stock is now $22.84. The sell-side median price target is $34 (stockanalysis, 2026-10-13).

findings.finding: RVIA's fall RV RoadSigns (ITR Economics, published 2026-10-16) cut the calendar-2026 North American wholesale forecast to ~290,000 units (range 284.6-295.4k), the bottom of the 290-310k that WGO's FY26 guide assumes, and forecasts 2027 flat to down at ~285,000 (274.7-295.3k). FY27 consensus has WGO revenue +3.7% to $2.82B and adj EPS +34% to $2.39 (stockanalysis, 14 analysts, as of 10-13), so a first FY27 guide built on RVIA's industry number would most likely put its revenue midpoint at or below consensus. Thor (2026-09-22) declined to give FY27 guidance at all and called the retail environment 'relatively flat'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is what moves this stock. The first FY26 guide on 2025-10-22 ($2.00-2.70 adj EPS against roughly $2.24 consensus) brought +28.53%. The 2026-06-25 guide cut (adj EPS $1.65-2.00 from $2.10-2.80, with a Q3 miss of $0.66 against $0.76) still brought +13.24%. The 2025-06-05 pre-announcement brought -5.99%. This name has bought its guide resets when it came in depressed.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus was last updated 10-13, before the RVIA revision, and it still models FY27 revenue growth while the industry body models flat-to-down units. If the market fully held a below-consensus guide, the sell-side numbers would have moved down. On the other hand the stock (-19% in 20 days, 9.5x consensus FY27 EPS) and the put skew already lean this way, so a good part of this is likely priced. That is why it is sized well below the implied move.
findings.independence: Thor's Q4 FY26 release, 2026-09-22 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000730263/000073026326000028/thoq4fy26-earningsrelease.htm): FY27 guidance withheld and 'relatively flat retail' expected. LCI cut its 2026 wholesale view to 280-300k at Q2 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/lci-industries-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-08/). Both are industry proxies; the company has not confirmed anything about FY27.

findings.finding: Thor, the largest peer, reported after WGO last spoke (2026-09-22, quarter to July 31). Its North American towable order backlog was $916.6M, up 74.6% year on year, and independent-dealer towable inventory was down 16.0% year on year. Its motorized backlog was down 27.5% and motorized gross margin fell 600 bp. Read across, a lean towable channel restocking would help WGO's FY27 towable outlook, and motorhome (WGO's largest segment, $320.7M in Q3) is the weaker side.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No WGO-specific history on peer read-throughs. Industry dealer-inventory commentary has moved RV names together before (for example the 2018 Northcoast 'unsustainable inventory' call took WGO down 8.4% in a day).
findings.why_not_priced: WGO has fallen about 19% since Thor's release instead of following its restocking signal, so the market is not reading Thor's towable backlog across to WGO. WGO's own June call partly explains why: Happe called MY27 dealer uptake 'one of the slower uptakes', said Grand Design faces 'targeted pressure' in fifth wheels, and WGO's towable dealer inventory was +5.5% at 2026-05-30 while Thor's fell. That company-level evidence counts against this proxy, so the finding is sized small. It is net positive only for the towable segment (about 40% of revenue) and slightly negative for motorhome.
findings.independence: RVIA (https://rv-pro.com/?p=125754): retail registrations have outpaced wholesale over the past 12 months, which also says the channel is lean. The Q3 transcript (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/WGO/Q32026) points the other way for WGO specifically.

findings.finding: On the Q3 call the CFO guided Q4 gross and EBITDA margins 'flattish to last year' (Q4 FY25 adj EBITDA $38.2M, 4.9% of $777.3M revenue). Applied to the ~$665M revenue consensus, that implies about $32-34M of adj EBITDA, which I estimate at about $0.52-0.57 adj EPS on 28.2M shares, ~$8M of D&A and ~$6M of interest, against consensus of $0.46-0.50. The revenue side is at risk of a small miss: industry wholesale for Jun-Aug was -14.0% for towables and -13.1% for motorhomes (RVIA monthly), and WGO towables have lagged the industry (-26.1% in Q3), so my segment build gives about $640-675M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name's quarter beats and misses have not set the sign. The Q2 FY26 beat was sold (-6.87%, reportedly on pricing concerns). The Q3 FY26 miss ($0.66 against $0.76) went up +13.24% on the guide. Q1 FY26 ($0.38 against $0.12) rose +8.43% with a guide raise.
findings.why_not_priced: It lands inside what the company already guided (Q4 implied $0.34-0.69), so it is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect, and the fiscal year it closes is already in the past. If the market were pricing a margin-driven EPS beat, consensus would sit above the guide midpoint ($0.515) and not at or below it.
findings.independence: RVIA's monthly wholesale data for June, July and August 2026 (https://rv-pro.com/news/rvia-august-rv-shipments-down-16-4-yoy/ ; https://sgbonline.com/report-u-s-july-2026-rv-shipments-post-moderating-segment-decliners-and-gainers/) covers the revenue side only. The EPS inference is my own arithmetic on a document.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-14 WGO announced it is closing its Lake Mills, IA Type B plant and its Middlebury, IN Winnebago Towables campus, consolidating them into Forest City and into a Grand Design plant, with both sites to be sold. No savings figure or charge was disclosed. The Q3 call promised 'more to announce' on towable capacity, and the release says the benefit comes 'as we move through fiscal 2027'. The Q4 release is the first place a dollar figure can land in the FY27 guide; Thor attached a >$100M annual savings figure to its own restructuring.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior quantified restructuring at a WGO print in the baseline window. SG&A fell 5.4% in Q3 on cost actions, and the June guide-cut quarter rose 13%.
findings.why_not_priced: The closures were public two months ago, so the fact itself is priced. Only a dollar amount, if WGO gives one, would be new, and no estimate source has one. That is why the size is small. Restructuring charges in Q4 GAAP EPS are a below-the-line one-off and are excluded from the adjusted EPS the stock trades on.
findings.independence: Iowa WARN notices for Forest City specialty-vehicle cuts were reported via aggregators (https://www.layofftracker.us/layoffs/company/winnebago-industries/2026), which is weak. Shares a theme with the guidance finding but not its document.

findings.finding: Positioning going into the print: spot $22.84 is down 19.2% in 20 sessions and about 30% since the CEO's $32.68 sale on 2026-08-13, sits 0.7% above the 52-week low, and short interest rose 5.5% to 9.99% of float (4.2 days to cover) at 2026-09-30. The two most recent guide events on a de-rated stock were bought hard (+28.5%, +13.2%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: +28.53% (2025-10-22) and +13.24% (2026-06-25) on guide events into weak tapes. The baseline's last 8 prints are 4 up and 4 down, with a median absolute move of 8.27%.
findings.why_not_priced: Skew is +5.9 points toward downside and the tape has fallen steadily, so the market expects bad news. If the market expected a relief rally, the skew would be flat or call-side. I found no company-specific cause for the October leg down, and an unexplained drawdown is not evidence of an overreaction, so this is sized small. 10% of float is moderate, not a crowded short.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline (run-up, skew), and the Form 4 for the CEO's 10b5-1 sale price (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000107687/000180809626000006/form4-08312026_020830.xml).

baseline_tension: The main negative (an FY27 guide likely below stale consensus) agrees with the +5.9 put skew and the -19% run-up, so it is probably largely priced. The small positives (Thor's channel restock, cost savings, Q4 margins, a washed-out tape) cut against the skew. Net, the evidence is balanced and p_up sits at 49.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (sign agreeing with the skew is likely priced; the reaction history on guide resets is positive): guidance finding -2.0 -> -1.5.
Rules 3 and 5 (my own caveat, WGO's slow MY27 uptake and towable share pressure in its own transcript, undercuts the Thor proxy): Thor read-through +1.0 -> +0.5.
Rule 6 (lands inside what the company already guided): Q4 margin/EPS finding +0.5 -> +0.3.
Rule 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth ~0; short interest is moderate, not crowded): positioning +1.5 -> +0.5.
Cost-savings finding +0.5 -> +0.3: announced in August and unquantified, so only a dollar figure would be new.
abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged (11 / 49): the lessons moved the findings, not the scaled number.
